s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and pelvic mass with associated lymphedema
salient_findings: Right lower abdominal pain
Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
Firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant
Multiple uterine fibroids
Large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
key_facts: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
Afebrile, blood pressure 110/80 mmHg, pulse 88 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Cardiac and respiratory examinations were unremarkable
Neurologic exam was normal
Abdomen revealed a firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
Bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass
Baseline hematologic, biochemical, thyroid, renal, and HIV/HBV/HCV serologies were within normal limits
Tumor markers were all in the reference range
Pap smear was negative
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion
Bilateral ovaries were not visualized separately
The uterus was bulky with multiple fibroids
Multiple small mesenteric lymph nodes were seen
Incidentally, a double inferior vena cava was identified

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Concerning imaging findings for ovarian neoplasm and presence of a large pelvic mass

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa and solid-cystic lesion on CT scan

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to ovarian cystadenocarcinoma and possibility of malignant transformation

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common type of ovarian cancer and presence of a large pelvic mass

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of pelvic mass and adnexal lesion, although less likely given the patient's age and clinical presentation

raw.rationale: The patient's tumor markers are within the reference range and the imaging findings show a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion, which is more characteristic of a benign ovarian tumor such as an ovarian cystadenoma.

rejected.label: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The normal tumor markers and the well-marginated appearance of the lesion on imaging make a malignant tumor like ovarian cystadenocarcinoma less likely.

rejected.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to suggest a mucinous subtype of ovarian cancer, and the tumor markers are normal.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to other malignant options, the lack of elevated tumor markers and the benign appearance on imaging make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: The size and the solid-cystic components of the lesion are not typical for a dermoid cyst, which usually presents as a well-defined, cystic mass with echogenic components due to the presence of sebaceous material, hair, or teeth.
